title: Finding ids and fates

ground.note: The brief: why (knowledge index use 3), what the records hold today (51 code-review findings, compliance findings, 68 review-fix commits, none linked), the eight settled decisions and the five open questions.
Use 3, escapes: join a finding's lens and escape to its fate; the data gap is a finding id and a disposition.

The code-review answer and file are one strict shape, `{ $schema, findings }`, each finding with severity, file, line, message, lens, escape, criterion, suggestion; no id. A rerun of the review overwrites the run folder's file.
perPhase[].findings[] carry dimension, severity (info, deviation, concern) and message; no id. Answer and file are one strict shape.
A review record is keyed `<runId>/<review>` on phax/records/v1 and carries the review's file byte for byte plus a manifest.
How a review record is committed to phax/records/v1 (trailers Run-Id, Review) and how a failed record write degrades to a warning naming a retry.
The headless code review writes code-review.json into the run folder, replacing any earlier one, then records it.
The decided-verdict shape: kind, chosen, abandoned, why, advocate, principles, reversibility, by (operator), at, revised.
The decision record manifest beside phase, authoring and review records; its id is the Decision-Id trailer.
Phase and review-fix commits carry the Short-Name trailer; release notes fold Short-Name commits into their run.
A run waiting for human review is in `review_open`.

Draft. §4 defines Finding id (`F<n>` review, `C<n>` compliance, run-unique, assigned by phax, numbering continued across passes) and outcomes fixed, open, dismissed, awaiting with an append-only decision history in the decided-verdict shape.
`--json` writes the command's versioned output contract on stdout, `$schema` first, and message lines on stderr.
The severity threshold: `info` is never planned and goes to the handoff note.

context:
phax records two kinds of review of a run. The headless code review (`phax review-code --headless`) writes `code-review.json` into the run folder and records it on `phax/records/v1` under `<runId>/code-review`. Each finding has `severity` (bug, deviation, concern, info), `file`, `line`, `message`, `lens`, `escape`, `criterion` and `suggestion`. The compliance review (`phax review-compliance`) writes `compliance-review.json` and records it under `<runId>/compliance-review`. Its findings sit in `perPhase[].findings[]`, each with `dimension`, `severity` (info, deviation, concern) and `message`. Both files are strict, `$schema`-stamped documents, and each is the session's answer as it came. Neither finding carries an id. A second review of the same run replaces the file in the run folder, and the records branch keeps the earlier one in its history.

In the phax repository on 2026-11-04 the records held 10 headless code reviews with 51 findings (bug 4, deviation 9, concern 25, info 13; escapes: untestable 19, omission 12, unexplored-input 9, fake-drift 5, same-author 5, weakened 1) and 10 compliance reviews. Since September, 68 review-fix commits on `main` carry `Short-Name: <run>` and no `Run-Id`. Their bodies are free bullets, and nothing links a commit to the finding it addresses.

The operator's flow today: the review runs while the run is `review_open`. The operator addresses the findings by hand in the run's final worktree (`phax enter`) and lands them all in one commit.

phax already writes and reads the trailers `Run-Id`, `Phase-Id`, `Short-Name`, `Decision-Id` and `Authoring-Id`. Artifact transitions (`phax artifact approve` and the others) make a path-scoped commit of exactly what they wrote, with a clean-file precondition. `phax artifact decide` stamps a decided verdict: chosen, abandoned, why, advocate, principles, reversibility, by, at, revised.

The Draft headless-review spec (2026-09-25) already defines a **Finding id**: run-unique, assigned by phax, `F<n>` for review findings and `C<n>` for compliance findings, numbering continued across passes. It also defines finding **outcomes** (fixed, open, dismissed, awaiting) with an append-only history in the decided-verdict shape. Only its headless code review has shipped. This spec takes the id and the fate on their own, without `review-plan` or `run --append`.
problem:
A review finding is a line in a JSON file that nobody follows up. It has no stable name, so no commit, record or person can point at it. Its fate (fixed, and by which change; judged wrong, and by whom and why; handed to later work; or simply left) lives only in the operator's memory. The 68 review-fix commits cannot be joined to the 51 findings they answered.

The knowledge index needs this join for its third use: teaching phax's agents the doctrine so they stop repeating errors ("last time a test like this missed, what did the better test look like?"). It can already read why the tests missed a finding (`lens`, `escape`). It cannot read what became of the finding. Without that, a recurring escape cannot be told apart from one that was fixed by a better test, and steme has no signal to promote a pattern into a guarantee. No public dataset pairs review findings with their outcome either: 68% of rejected agent PRs carry no stated reason.

Recording a fate by hand would not survive. A trailer the operator must type is a trailer that is forgotten. So the fate has to be a by-product of how the operator already works.

productGoal.statement: Every finding phax records gets a stable, run-unique id that phax assigns, and always has a fate from a closed set. phax writes each fate as a record on the records branch. The operator's fix becomes one phax command: the operator names the finding ids and the changed paths, and phax composes the commit (trailers, default subject) and the fate record, so the history builds itself while the operator works. The fates of a run's findings can be read through the CLI, in text for the operator and as a versioned `--json` answer for the knowledge index. The run's PR description lists the findings as they stood when the PR was created, and each finding settled afterwards gets a PR comment naming its new fate and what settles it. Git stays the source of truth: every fate can be rebuilt from the run branch, `main` and `phax/records/v1`.
productGoal.guidingRule: No finding is dropped: phax names it, the operator or a machine settles it through a phax command, and Git remembers how.

terminology.definition: One entry of a run's review: a code-review finding (in `code-review.json`) or a compliance finding (in `perPhase[].findings[]` of `compliance-review.json`, any severity). Findings the operator raises by hand are not findings in this slice.

As in the headless-review spec: a run-unique id that phax assigns when it persists a review. `F<n>` for a code-review finding and `C<n>` for a compliance finding, with n from 1. A later review of the same run continues the numbering, and an id is never reused within a run. The review session never writes an id. With the run's short name, it names a finding across the repository.

A finding's current state, one of a closed set: `open`, `fixed`, `dismissed`, `deferred`, `unrecorded`. It is what the headless-review spec calls the finding's outcome. That spec's `awaiting` is not part of this set and stays that spec's addition.
The fate of a finding whose review carries ids and that has no fate record yet. A new finding is `open`.
The finding's latest fate record is a fix. A fix names the commit that fixed the finding and that commit's path classes. A finding may be fixed by several commits over time.
The finding's latest fate record is a dismissal: the operator judged it wrong or not worth acting on, and gave a reason. Only an operator dismisses.
The finding's latest fate record is a deferral: the operator handed it to later work and named the brief, spec or `NEXT_STEPS.md` that takes it over. Only an operator defers.

The fate of a finding whose review was persisted before finding ids existed and that has no fate record yet. Such a finding gets its id lifted by position (`F1`… or `C1`… in document order). phax never guesses its fate. The same commands can set one later.

One entry on `phax/records/v1` that sets a finding's fate (fix, dismissal or deferral), stamped with by and at. Fate records are append-only, and the latest one decides the fate. All of a finding's fate records, oldest first, are its history.

A comment on a run's pull request, posted by `phax publish-pr`, that names one finding settled after the PR was opened, its new fate, and what settles it: the fixing commit or commits, the dismissal's reason, or the deferral's pointer.

The kind of each path a fixing commit changes, from the closed set `tests`, `gate-config`, `docs`, `code`. phax derives it deterministically from the path alone, never with a model. A fix records the set of classes its commit touched, which is "how it was fixed".
The worktree of the run's last phase, the one `phax enter` opens and `phax path` prints, where the operator works while the run is `review_open`.

requirements.title: phax assigns finding ids when it persists a review
requirements.statement: WHEN the system persists a code review or a compliance review of a run THE system SHALL give each of its findings a finding id, `F<n>` for a code-review finding and `C<n>` for a compliance finding, numbered after the highest id of that kind the run has already been given.

requirements.title: The review session never names an id
requirements.statement: IF a code-review or compliance-review session's answer carries an `id` on a finding THEN the system SHALL refuse the answer as it refuses any unknown key, naming the offending path.

requirements.title: Ids are written into the review files
requirements.statement: The system shall write each finding's id into `code-review.json` and `compliance-review.json` under a new `$schema` stamp, and record those files on `phax/records/v1` as it does today.

requirements.title: Older reviews get ids by position and the unrecorded fate
requirements.statement: WHEN the system reads a review persisted before finding ids existed THE system SHALL give its findings ids by position in document order (`F1`… for code-review findings; `C1`… across `perPhase` in order for compliance findings) and the fate `unrecorded` unless a fate record sets one, without rewriting the stored file.

requirements.title: Every finding has a fate from the closed set
requirements.statement: The system shall give every finding of a run exactly one fate from `open`, `fixed`, `dismissed`, `deferred`, `unrecorded`: the fate of its latest fate record, else `open` for a finding persisted with its id and `unrecorded` for a finding whose id was lifted.

requirements.title: A later review drops no finding
requirements.statement: WHEN a later review of the same run replaces the review file in the run folder THE system SHALL keep every earlier finding of that run, with its id, its fate and its fate records, readable through `phax finding list`.

requirements.title: List a run's findings with their fates
requirements.statement: WHEN `phax finding list <run>` runs THE system SHALL print every finding of the run with its id, source, severity, location, message and current fate, and for a `fixed` finding its fixing commits, for a `dismissed` finding its reason, and for a `deferred` finding its pointer.

requirements.title: The list is a versioned answer
requirements.statement: WHERE `--json` is given to a `phax finding` command THE system SHALL write its output contract as a `$schema`-stamped document per the command-contracts spec, carrying for each finding its fields, its current fate and its full history of fate records.

requirements.title: The fix command composes exactly one commit
requirements.statement: WHEN `phax finding fix <run> <id>… -- <path>…` runs THE system SHALL make one commit on the run branch in the run's final worktree, holding exactly the changes of the named paths, with one `Short-Name: <short-name>` trailer and one `Finding: <id>` trailer per id named, and leave every other staged or unstaged change in place.

requirements.title: A fix writes its fate records
requirements.statement: WHEN the fix command has made its commit THE system SHALL commit to `phax/records/v1` one fate record per id named, setting the fate `fixed` with that commit's sha, its path classes, `by` and `at`.

requirements.title: The fix command refuses an incomplete call
requirements.statement: IF the fix command names no path, names a path with no change, or names an id the run does not have THEN the system SHALL make no commit and no record, and exit non-zero naming the missing path, the unchanged path or the unknown id.

requirements.title: Fixes ride the run while it is open for review
requirements.statement: IF the fix command targets a run that is not `review_open` THEN the system SHALL refuse it, naming the run's state, and make no commit and no record.

requirements.title: How it was fixed is derived from paths
requirements.statement: The system shall classify each path of a fixing commit into exactly one of `tests`, `gate-config`, `docs`, `code` by a deterministic rule on the path, and record the set of classes the commit touched with the fix.

requirements.title: An operator dismisses with a reason
requirements.statement: WHEN `phax finding dismiss <run> <id>… --why <reason>` runs THE system SHALL commit to `phax/records/v1` one fate record per id setting the fate `dismissed`, carrying a decided verdict that chooses `dismiss`, abandons `fix` and `defer`, gives the reason as `why`, and is stamped with the operator's name and the time.

requirements.title: An operator defers to named later work
requirements.statement: WHEN `phax finding defer <run> <id>… --to <path> --why <reason>` runs THE system SHALL commit to `phax/records/v1` one fate record per id setting the fate `deferred`, carrying the pointer, the reason, and the operator's name and the time.

requirements.title: Dismissal and deferral refuse an incomplete call
requirements.statement: IF a dismiss or defer call lacks a reason, a deferral's `--to` names no file tracked at the checkout's HEAD, or an id is unknown to the run THEN the system SHALL write no record and exit non-zero naming what is missing or unknown.

requirements.title: A machine fixes but never dismisses or defers
requirements.statement: IF `phax finding dismiss` or `phax finding defer` is given `--by machine:<grant>` THEN the system SHALL refuse the call, naming that only an operator settles a finding without fixing it.

requirements.title: Who set a fate is stamped
requirements.statement: The system shall stamp every fate record with `by`, either `{ kind: operator, name }` from the committing Git identity or `{ kind: machine, grant }` from `--by machine:<grant>` on `fix`, and with `at`, an ISO-8601 UTC timestamp. Without a terminal, `--by` is required, as on `phax artifact approve`.

requirements.title: A fate needs the records branch
requirements.statement: IF records are off for the project THEN `phax finding fix`, `dismiss` and `defer` SHALL refuse before any commit, naming the records configuration.

requirements.title: A fate record that fails to commit is reported
requirements.statement: IF a fate record cannot be committed to `phax/records/v1` THEN the system SHALL exit non-zero and state that the fate is not recorded. For a fix, it SHALL also keep the fixing commit and name the command that records the fate for that commit.

requirements.title: The run's PR description lists findings by fate at creation
requirements.statement: WHEN the system creates a run's pull request THE system SHALL write into its description a findings section that names each `open` and `deferred` finding (id, severity, location, message, and the pointer for a deferred one) and counts the `fixed` and `dismissed` ones as they stand at creation, and SHALL never rewrite that description afterwards.

requirements.title: A finding settled after the PR opened gets a PR comment
requirements.statement: WHEN `phax publish-pr <run>` pushes the run branch of a run whose pull request already exists THE system SHALL post on that pull request one fate comment for each fate record set since the PR was opened that has no comment yet, naming the finding, its new fate and what settles it: the fixing commit or commits, the dismissal's reason, or the deferral's pointer.

requirements.title: A fate is commented once
requirements.statement: IF a fate record already has its fate comment on the run's pull request THEN a later `phax publish-pr <run>` SHALL post no further comment for it.

requirements.title: Fate commands stay local
requirements.statement: The system shall make no GitHub call from `phax finding list`, `fix`, `dismiss` or `defer`, so each works offline.

requirements.title: Findings never block
requirements.statement: The system shall not refuse or delay a run's completion, publication or merge because of a finding's fate.

surface.summary: Each code-review finding now carries a stable `id` such as `F3` that commits, records and people can point at.
Each compliance finding now carries a stable `id` such as `C2`, numbered across phases in document order.
Running `phax finding list <run>` shows every finding of a run with its id and fate, so you can pick the ids to fix, dismiss or defer.

surface.summary: An operator can mark one or more findings dismissed with a required reason, stamped with their name and the time.

surface.summary: Each fate of a finding is a record on the records branch, so the history of every finding can be rebuilt from Git alone.
A fixing commit names the findings it fixes in `Finding:` trailers beside `Short-Name`, so a commit joins to its findings from Git alone.

nonGoals: `phax review-plan`, `phax run --append`, review loops, and the `awaiting` fate: these stay in the headless-review spec, which reuses this spec's ids, fates and fate records instead of redefining them.
The knowledge index itself, its queries, and steme guarantees.
Classifying a fix with a model: path classes are derived from paths alone.
Blocking or delaying a run's completion, publication or merge on open findings.
Findings the operator raises by hand (follow-up `phax review add`).
Guessing the fate of findings reviewed before this change from existing commit messages: they are `unrecorded` until a command sets them.
Rewriting stored review files or records of earlier runs: older reviews get their ids when phax reads them, with no migration step.
Fixing a finding after the run is merged, on `main` (follow-up; see the open question on where the commands run).
A `Run-Id` trailer on fixing commits: they keep `Short-Name` only, so release notes fold them into their run as today.
Rewriting a pull request's description after it was created: later fates reach the PR as comments only.

acceptanceCriteria.name: A new code review gets F ids
acceptanceCriteria.given: a run with no earlier code review
acceptanceCriteria.when: `phax review-code <run> --headless` persists an answer of three findings
acceptanceCriteria.then: `code-review.json` carries the new `$schema` stamp and the findings have `id` `F1`, `F2`, `F3` in answer order, and the review record on `phax/records/v1` holds the same file

acceptanceCriteria.name: Compliance findings get C ids across phases
acceptanceCriteria.given: a compliance answer with one finding in phase-01 and two in phase-02
acceptanceCriteria.then: the findings have `id` `C1` (phase-01), `C2` and `C3` (phase-02) in `compliance-review.json`

acceptanceCriteria.name: A session that writes ids is refused
acceptanceCriteria.given: a code-review session whose answer has `"id": "F1"` on a finding
acceptanceCriteria.then: the answer is refused naming `findings[0].id` as an unexpected key, and no `code-review.json` is written

acceptanceCriteria.name: A second review continues the numbering and drops nothing
acceptanceCriteria.given: a run whose first code review gave F1–F3 and where F2 is recorded `fixed`
acceptanceCriteria.when: a second headless code review of the run persists two findings
acceptanceCriteria.then: they get `F4` and `F5`, and `phax finding list <run>` lists F1–F5 with F2 still `fixed` and F1, F3, F4, F5 `open`

acceptanceCriteria.name: An older review lists as unrecorded
acceptanceCriteria.given: a run whose `code-review.json` and `compliance-review.json` were persisted before finding ids existed
acceptanceCriteria.then: its code-review findings list as `F1`… and its compliance findings as `C1`… in document order, each with fate `unrecorded`, and neither stored file has changed

acceptanceCriteria.name: An unrecorded finding can be settled later
acceptanceCriteria.given: an older run whose finding F2 is `unrecorded`
acceptanceCriteria.when: `phax finding dismiss <run> F2 --why "superseded by the gate rework"` runs
acceptanceCriteria.then: `phax finding list <run>` shows F2 `dismissed` with that reason

acceptanceCriteria.name: The list names fates and their details
acceptanceCriteria.given: a run with an open, a fixed, a dismissed and a deferred finding
acceptanceCriteria.then: each finding prints with its id, severity, location, message and fate; the fixed one shows its commit and path classes, the dismissed one its reason, and the deferred one its pointer

acceptanceCriteria.name: The list answers a versioned document
acceptanceCriteria.given: the same run
acceptanceCriteria.then: stdout is one document with `$schema` first whose `findings[]` carry `id`, `source`, `fate` and `history`, the history holding every fate record oldest first, and stderr holds only message lines

acceptanceCriteria.name: Fix commits exactly the named paths with trailers
acceptanceCriteria.given: a `review_open` run whose final worktree has changes in `tests/gate.test.ts` and `src/app/gate.ts`, and an unrelated staged change in `README.md`
acceptanceCriteria.when: `phax finding fix <run> F2 F5 -- tests/gate.test.ts` runs
acceptanceCriteria.then: HEAD of the run branch is one new commit changing only `tests/gate.test.ts`, its message carries `Short-Name: <short-name>`, `Finding: F2` and `Finding: F5`, and `src/app/gate.ts` and the staged `README.md` change are still uncommitted

acceptanceCriteria.name: Fix records the fate with path classes
acceptanceCriteria.given: the fix above succeeded
acceptanceCriteria.then: F2 and F5 are `fixed`, each with a fate record naming the new commit, `pathClasses` `["tests"]`, `by` the operator and an `at` timestamp

acceptanceCriteria.name: Path classes are deterministic
acceptanceCriteria.given: a fixing commit that changes a test file, a source file and a Markdown file under `docs/`
acceptanceCriteria.then: `pathClasses` is exactly `["code", "docs", "tests"]`, and recording the same commit again yields the same set

acceptanceCriteria.name: Fix refuses a call that names no change
acceptanceCriteria.given: a `review_open` run with finding F2 and a clean `docs/gates.md`
acceptanceCriteria.when: `phax finding fix <run> F2` (no path), `phax finding fix <run> F2 -- docs/gates.md`, and `phax finding fix <run> F9 -- src/app/gate.ts` run
acceptanceCriteria.then: each exits non-zero naming respectively that no path was given, `docs/gates.md` as unchanged, and `F9` as unknown, and the run branch and `phax/records/v1` have no new commit

acceptanceCriteria.name: Fix refuses a run that is not open for review
acceptanceCriteria.given: a run in state `running`
acceptanceCriteria.then: it exits non-zero naming the state `running`, and nothing is committed

acceptanceCriteria.name: A machine may fix
acceptanceCriteria.given: a non-interactive caller and a `review_open` run with a change in `src/app/gate.ts`
acceptanceCriteria.when: `phax finding fix <run> F1 --by machine:review-bot -- src/app/gate.ts` runs
acceptanceCriteria.then: the fate record of F1 has `by` `{ kind: machine, grant: review-bot }`; the same call without `--by` and without a terminal is refused

acceptanceCriteria.name: Dismissal is a stamped decided verdict
acceptanceCriteria.given: a run with open finding F3
acceptanceCriteria.when: `phax finding dismiss <run> F3 --why "the second check guards --resume"` runs
acceptanceCriteria.then: a fate record on `phax/records/v1` sets F3 `dismissed` with a decided verdict choosing `dismiss`, abandoning `fix` and `defer`, `why` equal to the reason, `revised` empty, and `by` the operator with an `at` timestamp

acceptanceCriteria.name: Deferral names its successor
acceptanceCriteria.given: a run with open finding F5 and a tracked `docs/briefs/gate-retry-docs.md`
acceptanceCriteria.when: `phax finding defer <run> F5 --to docs/briefs/gate-retry-docs.md --why "docs pass after the gate rework"` runs
acceptanceCriteria.then: F5 is `deferred` with that pointer and reason, stamped by the operator

acceptanceCriteria.name: Dismiss and defer refuse incomplete calls
acceptanceCriteria.given: a run with finding F5
acceptanceCriteria.when: `phax finding dismiss <run> F5` without `--why`, `phax finding defer <run> F5 --to docs/briefs/nope.md --why x` where the file is untracked, and `phax finding dismiss <run> F9 --why x` run
acceptanceCriteria.then: each exits non-zero naming the missing reason, the untracked pointer, or the unknown id, and no fate record is written

acceptanceCriteria.name: A machine cannot dismiss or defer
acceptanceCriteria.given: a run with open finding F3
acceptanceCriteria.when: `phax finding dismiss <run> F3 --by machine:review-bot --why x` runs
acceptanceCriteria.then: it exits non-zero saying only an operator dismisses a finding, and F3 stays `open`

acceptanceCriteria.name: Fate commands need records
acceptanceCriteria.given: a project with records off
acceptanceCriteria.then: each exits non-zero naming the records configuration, before any commit

acceptanceCriteria.name: A failed fate record is reported, the fix kept
acceptanceCriteria.given: a `review_open` run where committing to `phax/records/v1` fails
acceptanceCriteria.then: the fixing commit exists on the run branch, the command exits non-zero saying F2's fate is not recorded and naming the command that records it for that commit

acceptanceCriteria.name: The latest fate record decides, history keeps all
acceptanceCriteria.given: a finding F3 first dismissed, then fixed by a commit
acceptanceCriteria.then: F3's `fate` is `fixed` and its `history` holds the dismissal then the fix, oldest first

acceptanceCriteria.name: The PR description names open and deferred findings at creation
acceptanceCriteria.given: a run with findings open F4 and C1, deferred F5, fixed F1 and F2, dismissed F3, and no pull request yet
acceptanceCriteria.when: the run's pull request is created
acceptanceCriteria.then: its description has a findings section naming F4, C1 under Open and F5 with its pointer under Deferred, and reading `Fixed: 2 · Dismissed: 1`

acceptanceCriteria.name: A later publish leaves the description alone
acceptanceCriteria.given: a run whose pull request was created with F4 open, and F4 was then fixed by a commit
acceptanceCriteria.then: the pull request's description is unchanged and still lists F4 under Open

acceptanceCriteria.name: A finding settled later gets a comment at publish
acceptanceCriteria.given: a run whose pull request exists, where F2 was fixed by commit 9f8e7d6 and F3 dismissed with a reason after it was opened
acceptanceCriteria.then: the branch is pushed and the pull request gains one comment for F2 naming its new fate `fixed` and commit 9f8e7d6, and one for F3 naming `dismissed` and the reason, the commit being visible on the PR

acceptanceCriteria.name: A fate is commented only once
acceptanceCriteria.given: the publish above has posted the comments for F2 and F3, and F5 was then deferred
acceptanceCriteria.then: exactly one new comment appears, for F5 naming `deferred` and its pointer, and none for F2 or F3

acceptanceCriteria.name: Fate commands work offline
acceptanceCriteria.given: a machine with no network and no usable `gh`
acceptanceCriteria.then: each completes as without a pull request, and none calls GitHub

acceptanceCriteria.name: Open findings do not block
acceptanceCriteria.given: a run with open findings of severity `bug`
acceptanceCriteria.when: the run is completed and published
acceptanceCriteria.then: completion and publication proceed as with no findings

arbitratedQuestions.question: Which changes does `phax finding fix` commit?

options.label: Exactly the paths named after `--`; refuse when none is named or a named one has no change
options.abandons: the one-word call: the operator types the paths even when the worktree holds only this fix

options.label: Every uncommitted change in the run's final worktree
options.abandons: one finding per commit: whatever else was edited or staged rides along and is attributed to the named findings

options.label: Whatever is staged in the run's final worktree
options.abandons: phax composing the commit: the operator stages by hand again, and a stale stage is swept in silently

arbitratedQuestions.rationale: A precise join between a finding and the change that fixed it is the whole point. A commit that sweeps in unrelated edits corrupts the path classes and the knowledge index's lesson. Typing paths is cheap, and shell completion can offer the changed ones.

verdict.why: A precise join between a finding and the change that fixed it is the whole point. A commit that sweeps in unrelated edits corrupts the path classes and the knowledge index's lesson. Typing paths is cheap, and shell completion can offer the changed ones.
verdict.advocate: Committing every uncommitted change makes the call one word: when the worktree holds only this fix, naming paths is pure ceremony the operator repeats on every fix.

arbitratedQuestions.question: Where and when does `phax finding fix` run?

options.label: In the run's final worktree while the run is `review_open`, in this slice; dismiss and defer run on any run whose records exist
options.abandons: recording a fix made on `main` after the merge, which waits for a follow-up

options.label: Also on `main` after the merge, committing there with the run's trailers
options.abandons: a bounded slice: a second commit target, its own preconditions, and fixes outside the run's PR

arbitratedQuestions.rationale: The final worktree is where the operator fixes today, and the fix rides the run's PR. Dismissal and deferral write only a record, so older and merged runs, `unrecorded` ones included, can still be settled.

verdict.why: The final worktree is where the operator fixes today, and the fix rides the run's PR. Dismissal and deferral write only a record, so older and merged runs, `unrecorded` ones included, can still be settled.
verdict.advocate: Allowing fixes on main after the merge covers findings noticed late, which is when many of them are fixed, instead of leaving those fixes unrecorded.

arbitratedQuestions.question: Which command family carries list, fix, dismiss and defer?

options.label: A `phax finding list|fix|dismiss|defer <run> <id>…` group
options.abandons: grouping by workflow next to `review-code` and `review-compliance`: one more top-level noun

options.label: Verbs under `review` (`phax review fix …`)
options.abandons: the noun the index and the doctrine use; `review` today names sessions that produce findings, not what becomes of them

options.label: Verbs under `records` (`phax records finding …`)
options.abandons: the operator's flow: `records` reads and syncs what phax wrote, while `fix` makes a code commit on the run branch

arbitratedQuestions.rationale: `finding` is the noun every reader of this data uses. It keeps code-changing `fix` out of `records`, and `--json` comes with each command under command-contracts.

verdict.why: `finding` is the noun every reader of this data uses. It keeps code-changing `fix` out of `records`, and `--json` comes with each command under command-contracts.
verdict.advocate: Verbs under `review` keep the operator's workflow together beside `review-code` and `review-compliance`, with no new top-level noun to learn.

arbitratedQuestions.question: What commit subject does `phax finding fix` write?

options.label: phax writes `fix(review): F2, F5 of <short-name>`, `-m` overrides the subject and an optional body follows; trailers and the record are always phax's
options.abandons: a descriptive subject by default: `git log --oneline` reads as ids until the operator passes `-m`

options.label: `-m <subject>` is required
options.abandons: the one-step call: every fix needs a written subject, and agents invent filler

options.label: phax derives a subject from the findings' messages
options.abandons: a deterministic, short subject: finding messages are long and phrased as problems, not changes

arbitratedQuestions.rationale: The operator decided that phax composes everything but the change. A default subject keeps the call one step, and `-m` is there when the operator wants the log to read well. Trailers stay out of the operator's hands either way.

verdict.why: The operator decided that phax composes everything but the change. A default subject keeps the call one step, and `-m` is there when the operator wants the log to read well. Trailers stay out of the operator's hands either way.
verdict.advocate: Requiring `-m` forces every fix to carry a subject that says what changed, so the log is readable from the start instead of a run of ids.

arbitratedQuestions.question: How does a later review of the same run keep earlier findings readable?

options.label: The run folder's file holds the latest review only; `phax finding list` reads earlier reviews from the records branch's history of the review's key
options.abandons: one file a reader can open to see every finding of the run; earlier findings need the records branch

options.label: The review file accumulates: a later review appends its findings after the earlier ones
options.abandons: the file as one review's answer: a compliance file would carry a verdict beside findings from an older review it no longer stands behind

arbitratedQuestions.rationale: Git is the source of truth, and fate commands already need the records branch. Keeping each file as one review's answer preserves what the compliance verdict means. Re-reviews of one run are rare.

verdict.why: Git is the source of truth, and fate commands already need the records branch. Keeping each file as one review's answer preserves what the compliance verdict means. Re-reviews of one run are rare.
verdict.advocate: An accumulating file lets a reader open one file to see every finding of the run, with no dependency on the records branch.

arbitratedQuestions.question: Can `phax finding fix` record a commit that already exists (for `unrecorded` findings and for a fate record that failed to commit)?

options.label: `phax finding fix <run> <id>… --commit <sha>` records an existing commit reachable from the run branch or `main`, with its path classes, and makes no new commit
options.abandons: one shape of fixing commit: a backfilled commit has no `Finding:` trailer and may hold several fixes, so its path classes are coarser

options.label: No: only a commit phax makes can fix a finding
options.abandons: settling the 51 existing findings as fixed, and retrying a failed fate record: they can only be dismissed, deferred or left `unrecorded`

arbitratedQuestions.rationale: The brief requires `unrecorded` findings to be settable later with the same commands, and most of the existing ones were fixed by one of the 68 review-fix commits. The operator names the commit, so phax still guesses nothing. The same flag is the retry for a fix whose record failed.

verdict.why: The brief requires `unrecorded` findings to be settable later with the same commands, and most of the existing ones were fixed by one of the 68 review-fix commits. The operator names the commit, so phax still guesses nothing. The same flag is the retry for a fix whose record failed.
verdict.advocate: Allowing only commits phax made keeps every fix one uniform shape, with a Finding trailer and exact path classes, instead of coarse backfilled records.

arbitratedQuestions.question: When does the PR's findings section follow fates set after the PR was opened?

options.label: Re-running `phax publish-pr <run>` pushes the branch and rewrites the findings section of an existing PR, leaving the rest of the body
options.abandons: a PR that is always current: it is stale until the operator publishes again

options.label: Each fate command updates the PR when one is open
options.abandons: fate commands that stay local: each needs the network and `gh`, and fails or warns offline

arbitratedQuestions.rationale: Fixes are pushed at publish time anyway. Keeping fate commands local keeps them fast, makes them work offline, and spares an agent calling them a network dependency.

verdict.why: A PR's description is written once, when the PR is created, and findings are settled after that. phax never rewrites the description: it keeps listing the findings as they stood at creation. Instead, each finding settled after the PR was opened gets one PR comment naming the finding, its new fate and what settles it (the fixing commit or commits, the dismissal's reason, or the deferral's pointer). The comments are posted when `phax publish-pr <run>` pushes the branch, so a fixing commit is already visible on the PR when its comment names it. Each settled finding is commented once: a later publish posts only fates not yet commented. Fate commands stay local and offline.
verdict.advocate: Rewriting the findings section at each publish keeps one always-readable summary in the description, instead of scattering the story across comments a reviewer must read in order.

arbitratedQuestions.question: How is the spec split into plans?

options.label: (1) ids: the review file shape cut, lifting older reviews to `unrecorded`, and `finding list`; (2) the fate commands and their records; (3) the PR findings section
options.abandons: one end-to-end run: the operator gets `finding list` before being able to set a fate

options.label: (1) ids and list; (2) fate commands and the PR section together
options.abandons: a small final plan: the PR body change rides with the largest plan and its review

arbitratedQuestions.rationale: Each plan ships something the operator can use and review on its own. Ids and the list come first because every later plan reads them.

verdict.why: Each plan ships something the operator can use and review on its own. Ids and the list come first because every later plan reads them.
verdict.advocate: Two plans mean fewer runs and reviews, and the PR section is too small to justify a plan of its own.

settled: phax assigns ids when it persists a review; the session never writes one. `F<n>` for code-review findings and `C<n>` for compliance findings (every severity), unique within the run and never reused.

Fates are exactly `open`, `fixed`, `dismissed`, `deferred`, `unrecorded`. A new finding is `open`. A finding from a review persisted before ids existed is `unrecorded`, with its id lifted by position.
Every fate is written by a command, as a fate record on `phax/records/v1` stamped with by and at. The latest record decides the fate, and records are append-only.
A machine may fix (`--by machine:<grant>`) but never dismisses or defers.
A dismissal carries a decided verdict (chosen `dismiss`, abandoned `fix` and `defer`, `revised` empty).
The fix command composes the commit: `Short-Name` plus one `Finding:` trailer per id, the named paths only, one commit per call.
Path classes are `tests`, `gate-config`, `docs`, `code`, derived deterministically from the path.

The PR description names open and deferred findings and counts fixed and dismissed ones as they stand at creation, and is never rewritten. A finding settled afterwards gets one PR comment, posted by `phax publish-pr` after it pushes the branch, once per fate. Fate commands never call GitHub. Nothing blocks.

The headless-review spec, when revived, reuses this spec's Finding id, fate set and fate records as its outcomes and history, adding only `awaiting`; its per-finding `outcome`/`history` fields in `code-review.json` are replaced by fate records.
The spec splits into three plans: (1) ids, the older-review lift to `unrecorded` and `finding list`; (2) the fate commands and their records; (3) the PR description and the fate comments.
open: The exact path-class rule (which globs are `tests`, which files are `gate-config`: `phax.json` and the gate tools' config files); it must give each path exactly one class and live in one place.

The fate record's key layout and manifest name on `phax/records/v1` (indicative `<runId>/finding/<id>/<NN>`, kind `finding-fate`), and whether one fix call writes its per-id records in one records commit.

For a dismissal's decided verdict: `advocate` (indicative: the finding's `suggestion`, its message for a compliance finding, as the strongest case for `fix`), `principles` (indicative: empty) and `reversibility` (indicative: `cheap`, since a later fate record can supersede it).
Exit codes of the refusals, within the existing families and declared per command-contracts.
How `phax finding fix` resolves paths: relative to the run's final worktree root, or to the current directory when it is inside that worktree.
How `phax publish-pr` knows which fate records already have a comment (for example a marker in the comment that it reads back through `gh`), so that a re-run posts only what is missing.
constraints: No back-compat shims: the review files' new shape requires `id`. Older files stay readable through the schema history readers and get their ids at read time, with no migration step and no rewrite of stored files.
Every new document (`finding-list` answer, fate record manifest, new review file stamps) is born with `$schema`.
All I/O through ports; the fix commit follows the artifact-transition pattern (path-scoped, `-o <paths>` semantics, never sweeping other staged changes).
Fate commands honor command-contracts: `--json` on each, message lines on stderr, refusal before any write.
Release notes keep folding fixing commits into their run by `Short-Name`; fixing commits carry no `Run-Id`.
A fate comment is posted only after the branch push, so a fixing commit it names is already visible on the PR.

docsPage.page: docs/findings.md — Review findings: ids and fates
docsPage.reader: An operator who has run a code or compliance review on a `review_open` run and now wants to address its findings: fix some, dismiss or defer others, and see what is left before publishing.
docsPage.example: Run `phax finding list gate-retry`. Fix the test, then run `phax finding fix gate-retry F2 -- tests/gate.test.ts`. Dismiss the duplicate-check finding with `phax finding dismiss gate-retry F3 --why "the second check guards --resume"`, defer the docs gap to a brief with `phax finding defer gate-retry F5 --to docs/briefs/gate-retry-docs.md --why …`, then `phax publish-pr gate-retry` and see one comment per settled finding on the PR, beside the description that listed the findings at creation.
